title: Makefile as a task runner
when: The user wants short commands such as make test or make run for a project, or a Makefile that rebuilds outputs only when sources change.
prompt:
Goal: A readable Makefile with phony tasks, real file targets where useful, and a self documenting help target.
Steps:
1. Set .DEFAULT_GOAL := help, SHELL := bash and .SHELLFLAGS := -eu -o pipefail -c so recipe errors stop make.
2. Declare .PHONY for every task that is not a file (help, run, test, clean).
3. Indent recipes with a real tab; join dependent commands with && or enable .ONESHELL.
4. Document targets with ## comments and a help target that greps them from $(MAKEFILE_LIST).
5. Overridable variables: PY ?= python3, NODE ?= node, OUT := dist.
6. Generated files get real rules with prerequisites (dist/app.css: src/*.css) and @mkdir -p $(@D); clean deletes only listed generated paths.
Quality bar:
- make alone prints help.
- Every recipe works from a fresh clone.
- Targets are plain verbs.
Pitfalls:
- Spaces instead of a tab ("missing separator").
- Expecting cd on one recipe line to affect the next.
- Wildcard clean rules that can delete sources.
Verify:
- [ ] .PHONY lists the tasks.
- [ ] help exists and is the default.
- [ ] Recipes start with tabs.
- [ ] Tools use ?= variables.
Output: Makefile at the project root and a Commands section in README.

examples.input: quero comandos curtos tipo make test e make run
examples.output: Makefile with help default, run, test, clean as .PHONY, PY ?= python3, ## comments
